description: {"time": 1783112251304, "blocks": [{"id": "vj9l4fy7z1", "data": {"text": "Pablo \u2014 named infamously after Pablo Escobar \u2014 patrols the Ongata Line Sacco routes with a notoriety that is hard to miss. Matatu culture has long flirted with outlaw imagery, and the Escobar motif is a recurring theme that speaks to the rebellious spirit of Nairobi's minibus scene. Dennis Muraguri's woodcut captures the stern portrait and bold typography with graphic precision. Far from glorifying crime, the Pablo design belongs to matatu culture's tradition of adopting antihero icons \u2014 a visual language that challenges respectability and embraces the street's own codes. Muraguri's reproduction translates this complex cultural reference into a collectable artwork that invites conversation. This print is for those who appreciate the edgier side of street art, or who collect works that document Nairobi's alternative visual culture.
